Chinese humanoid robots broke records set by humans, including Usain Bolt's 100m sprint world record, on the opening day of the Olympics-like World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing on Saturday. More than 2,000 humanoid robots were participating in the event, organisers said. In a 100-metre sprint, a humanoid robot achieved a result of 9.39 seconds, beating the human record of 9.58 seconds set by Jamaican athlete Bolt in 2009. In a standing high jump, a humanoid robot was able to reach 2.88m, well above the 0.95m best result by a humanoid in last year’s first edition of the games. It surpassed the human high jump record of 2.45m set by Cuba’s Javier Sotomayor in 1993. The five-day games, now in their second year, are a spectacle demonstrating China’s rapid progress in advanced robotics as the technology race with the US heats up. There are 51 events and more than 1,000 competitions taking place, including running, table tennis and football. For more news, visit @sbsnews_au (link in bio).

Figure did something absolutely wild with its retired humanoid robots. 🤯🔥 Instead of dismantling its F.02 fleet, Figure trained the robots to autonomously jump into a 75-ton electric arc furnace filled with molten steel in Imatra, Finland. And yes this was real. Figure says the robots were: 🤖 Trained to jump in simulation 🦘 Practiced with airbags at its San Jose campus 🏭 Sent to a foundry the team had never visited 🔥 Given only six furnace melts across 24 hours ⚡ Operating despite extreme heat and electromagnetic interference The reason? Figure wanted to decommission the F.02 fleet while protecting proprietary hardware and freeing engineering resources for its next-generation robots. The resulting metal bars are being turned into a limited series of F.02 commemorative artifacts. And there is a serious robotics story behind the crazy video: Figure had to train a jump policy that could transfer from simulation to a completely unfamiliar real-world environment and accurately land the robot in the furnace. Arnold Schwarzenegger was also involved after suggesting the robots should be melted an obvious nod to Terminator 2. This may be the most brutal robot retirement ever. 😅 Would you call this engineering genius or the most extreme robot disposal method ever? 👀 🏢 Company: Figure , Brett Adcock ⚠️ This content is shared for informational purposes only. videos.caption: I spent days teaching a 3D-printed robot duck to walk. Most of that time, it was falling over. It’s my own build of the Open Duck Mini. The open-source, BDX-inspired biped created by Antoine Pirrone. The whole thing is 3D-printed and runs on hobby-grade servos instead of industrial actuators, which is what makes it buildable on a normal budget and also what makes it so hard to get walking. The hard part wasn’t the printing or the assembly. It was the sim-to-real gap. A gait that walks perfectly in MuJoCo hits real-world joint slop, servo lag, and a center of mass that won’t sit still, and just before you know it, the duck face plants into the floor. It took me 40+ calibration passes before it could take three steps without tipping! What the build came down to: • 3D-printed chassis • Per-joint offset calibration (where most of the pain lived) • Policy training in simulation (MuJoCo / Isaac Lab) • Build guide + docs via Tnkr • A lot of failed walks Real hardware. Real failures. Real progress.

Tesla has deployed over 1,000 Optimus Gen 3 humanoid robots across its Gigafactory Texas and Fremont facilities, marking the first large-scale commercial use of general-purpose humanoid robotics in high-speed. The robots use a new FSD-v15 neural architecture and 22-degree-of-freedom hands to autonomously navigate factory floors and perform tasks like parts kitting on battery cell lines—learning from video of human workers rather than traditional programming. Competitors including Figure AI, backed by Microsoft and Nvidia, are accelerating rival deployments, while Tesla targets 50,000 units by year-end and has broken ground on an “Optimus Megafactory” in Austin. #tesla #optimus #gigafactory #nvidia #microsoft
